Steep contango = front-month IV is cheap relative to back-month; calendar spread profits as they converge. Tests whether the continuous slope level has predictive value for this convergence.
testability_notes: Data: daily_series.parquet — iv_30d, iv_60d. Slope = iv_60d - iv_30d (contango = positive). Top quintile: slope >= 80th percentile. Bottom quintile: slope <= 20th percentile. 5-day convergence: slope - slope.shift(-5). Positive convergence = slope moved toward flat = calendar spread profits. Primary metric: median_convergence_top - median_convergence_bottom. Mann-Whitney U. Cliff's delta. State clearly that this is a term-structure convergence proxy for actual calendar P&L — not actual options P&L.

title: First 30-Minute Option Volume Direction Predicts Rest-of-Day Price Direction
claim: Sessions where calls represent more than 60% of total option volume in the first 30 minutes of trading (9:30–10:00 AM) show a positive average return from 10:00 AM to close, while sessions where puts represent more than 60% show a negative average return from 10:00 AM to close — testing whether early option flow has directional information content.
rationale: The market open is the highest-liquidity window where overnight analysis translates to action. If early-session option flow has directional content rather than being purely hedging noise, it should show up as price continuation. Tests whether the call/put volume split in the first 30 minutes provides information beyond random hedging. High noise is expected — most option flow is hedging — but extreme readings (>60% in one direction) may contain signal.
testability_notes: Data: data/raw/chains/ — 2025 only, 5-min bars. Aggregate call and put volume from 9:30–10:00 AM per date. call_vol_pct = call_volume / (call_volume + put_volume). call_heavy: > 0.60. put_heavy: < 0.40. Databento 5-min bars for 10:00 AM price and close. ROD return = (close - price_10am) / price_10am. Primary metric: mean_rod_return_call_heavy - mean_rod_return_put_heavy. Mann-Whitney U. Cliff's delta. Report N per group — expect small N after 60% threshold filtering.

title: Thursday IV Term Structure Predicts Monday IV Direction (Weekly Expiry Roll Effect)
claim: The iv_60d − iv_30d slope reading on Thursdays predicts the direction of the following Monday's iv_30d change with better-than-chance accuracy (> 60% win rate), consistent with weekly expiry mechanics compressing Thursday's front-month IV surface and creating a systematic roll artifact that reverses on Monday.
rationale: Weekly expiry mechanics cause near-term vol surface compression on Thursdays as 0DTE theta accelerates and dealers shed expiring positions. This may create a systematic artifact where Thursday's iv_30d is artificially suppressed, making Monday's first reading appear as an increase — predictably exploitable as a calendar-mechanical signal. Tests whether the Thursday term structure reading has predictive value for Monday's IV direction specifically.
testability_notes: Data: daily_series.parquet — iv_30d, iv_60d, date. is_thursday = dayofweek == 3. For each Thursday, match to the following Monday's iv_30d change (Monday iv_30d - Thursday iv_30d). positive_slope_thu = slope > 0 (contango). Win = Thursday slope sign matches Monday iv change direction. Primary metric: win_rate (fraction of Thursdays where Thursday slope sign correctly predicts Monday IV direction). p_binomial vs 0.50 baseline. Report n_weeks. Expected N ~ 100 weeks in 2-year window.

title: Pattern 4 Episodes Cluster: IV Divergence Persists 3+ Consecutive Sessions
claim: When a Pattern 4 signal fires (iv_30d rising 5-day while realized vol flat/falling), the condition persists for at least 3 consecutive sessions in the majority (> 50%) of episodes, indicating that the first day of divergence is an early entry opportunity rather than a single-day noise event. Meaningful only if H53 is supported.
rationale: If Passarelli Pattern 4 is predictive (H53), the entry timing question is whether to act on day 1 or wait for confirmation. A clustering pattern (majority of episodes last 3+ days) means early entry catches more of the IV expansion and the range expansion window. A non-clustering pattern (mostly 1–2 day events) means the signal fires and resolves quickly, reducing its practical value as an early warning. This hypothesis quantifies episode structure to inform practical use.
testability_notes: Data: daily_series.parquet — iv_30d, log_return. Build same pattern4_mask as H53 (delta_iv > 0.005 AND delta_rv < 0.005 over 5-day windows). Count consecutive True runs in the mask. Primary metric: pct_runs_ge_3 = fraction of episodes lasting >= 3 consecutive days. Support: pct_runs_ge_3 > 0.50 AND n_runs >= 10. Reject: pct_runs_ge_3 <= 0.30. Also report median_run_length, mean_run_length, max_run_length, n_runs. NOTE: only meaningful if H53 is supported — state this explicitly in verdict_reason.

title: Opening Inside Put/Call Wall Range Predicts Session Containment
claim: When QQQ opens between the day's highest-OI put wall (highest put OI strike below underlying) and call wall (highest call OI strike above underlying), the session closes inside that same wall range more often than sessions where QQQ opens outside the wall range close inside an equivalent-width band centered on their open.
rationale: The Reddit 'How to Use Options Data' post identifies the put wall and call wall as the strikes with the highest near-term open interest concentration, acting as gravitational anchors for price during the session. Market makers who are net short options at these strikes must delta-hedge in ways that resist price moving through them — put walls create buying pressure on declines, call walls create selling pressure on advances. If QQQ opens inside this range, the session should be contained as those hedging flows push back from both walls.
testability_notes: Data: data/raw/chains/ param files (C and P, 2025-04-01 → 2025-12-31, 190 dates). Call wall = strike above underlying with highest total OI (dte 1-30). Put wall = strike below underlying with highest total OI (dte 1-30). Open price and close price from daily_series. Signal: open between put_wall and call_wall. Containment: close also between put_wall and call_wall. Primary metric: containment_rate_inside_opens - containment_rate_outside_opens. Mann-Whitney or binomial test on containment rates.

title: Opening Outside Put/Call Wall Range Predicts Same-Direction Continuation
claim: When QQQ opens above the call wall, the session is more likely to close above the call wall and finish positive for the day than a randomly selected session. When QQQ opens below the put wall, the session is more likely to close below the put wall and finish negative. Opening outside the wall range signals a breakout that lacks the gamma-suppression effect.
rationale: When price opens outside the put/call wall range, the market-maker delta-hedging pressure that normally constrains price within the range is absent or reversed. Above the call wall, dealers who were short calls must hedge by buying the underlying on further advances — creating momentum rather than resistance. This is the directional extension of H61: inside = containment, outside = continuation.
testability_notes: Same data as H61. Signal: open > call_wall (above) or open < put_wall (below). For above-open days: continuation = close > call_wall AND close > open (positive). For below-open days: continuation = close < put_wall AND close < open (negative). Primary metric: continuation_rate - 0.50 (binomial test vs chance). Report separately for above vs below. Also compute: mean return on continuation signal days vs inside-range days.

title: Rising Price With Rising Open Interest Predicts Next-Session Continuation
claim: Sessions where QQQ closes higher AND total option open interest increases overnight (comparing to prior day's param file) show stronger next-session continuation (positive next-day return more often) than sessions where QQQ closes higher but OI decreases. Rising price with rising OI signals real buying rather than short covering.
rationale: Classic open interest interpretation from technical analysis: rising price + rising OI = new money entering long positions = trend confirmation. Rising price + falling OI = shorts covering or longs reducing = trend weakening. The Investopedia OI interpretation table explicitly lists these four combinations and their conventional signals. Testing this empirically on QQQ option OI (which reflects total hedging and directional demand in the options market) provides a derivatives-market version of the classic stock OI signal.
testability_notes: Data: daily total OI (sum of all openinterest across all param file contracts for that date, C+P combined). Compute overnight OI change = today_total_OI - yesterday_total_OI. Signal: log_return > 0 (price rose) AND oi_change > 0 (OI rose). Control: log_return > 0 AND oi_change < 0 (price rose, OI fell). Outcome: next-session log_return. Primary metric: mean_next_return_rising_oi - mean_next_return_falling_oi (on up-days only). Mann-Whitney U. Data available on all 190 overlap dates minus first (for OI change).

title: Expiry Fridays Close Nearer Max Pain Than Opening Price
claim: On weekly expiry Fridays (dates where dte=0 options exist in chains data), QQQ's closing price is closer to the max pain strike than its opening price, more often than expected by chance. Max pain = the option strike where total expiring option dollar value is minimized.
rationale: Max pain theory holds that option writers (who are mostly market makers and institutions) collectively benefit when expiration settles near the strike that minimizes total payout. The force is mechanical: as expiry approaches, delta hedging of near-the-money options at the max pain strike creates price pressure toward it. H23 tested pin risk but had insufficient data — now the chains/ param files provide per-strike OI for max pain calculation directly.
testability_notes: Data: qqq_opts_by_param files. Identify expiry Fridays as dates where dte=0 options exist. For those dates: compute max pain = argmin over candidate strikes of [sum of put OI * max(0, strike - candidate) + call OI * max(0, candidate - strike)] across ALL strikes on that expiry date. Measure: dist_open = |open - max_pain|, dist_close = |close - max_pain|. Signal: dist_close < dist_open (price moved toward max pain during the session). Primary metric: fraction of expiry Fridays where dist_close < dist_open. Binomial test vs 0.50.

title: Overnight Wall Shifts in the Same Direction Predict Next-Session Return Direction
claim: When both the put wall and call wall shift upward overnight (today's put wall > yesterday's put wall AND today's call wall > yesterday's call wall), the next-session return is positive more often than on days when both walls shift downward. Coordinated wall shifts reflect market makers repositioning their largest hedging concentrations directionally.
rationale: The Reddit post explicitly states that wall shifts are directional signals — walls moving up indicate bullish repositioning of the largest OI concentrations. If the strikes with the most defensive hedging (put walls) and offensive exposure (call walls) both move higher overnight, the aggregate market-maker delta position has shifted bullish, which should manifest as positive next-day returns. Tests the Reddit post's directional claim about wall dynamics.
testability_notes: Data: consecutive-date wall calculations from param files. put_wall_D = highest-OI put strike below underlying on date D. call_wall_D = highest-OI call strike above underlying on date D. Wall shift = put_wall_D - put_wall_{D-1} and call_wall_D - call_wall_{D-1}. Both-up: both shifts > 0. Both-down: both shifts < 0. Outcome: next-session log_return from daily_series. Primary metric: mean_return_both_up - mean_return_both_down. Mann-Whitney U. Need consecutive trading days in the data.

title: Call Wall Intraday Resistance: Upper Shadow Ratio Test
claim: On sessions where the intraday high reaches within $5 of the call_wall (without breaching it), the upper shadow ratio (high - close) / (high - low) is larger than on sessions where the high stays more than $10 below the call_wall, consistent with dealer gamma selling creating a resistance ceiling at the dominant call strike concentration.
rationale: The call wall is the strike with the largest call-side open interest above the underlying. Dealers who sold those calls are long gamma and must sell the underlying as price rises toward the strike. This selling pressure should create a visible ceiling effect: sessions where price approaches the wall should show disproportionate high-to-close reversion relative to the session range. The upper shadow ratio (high - close) / (high - low) normalizes for move size so the wall effect is not confounded with large-move mean-reversion.
testability_notes: Data: daily_series.parquet (high, low, close) + wall table from qqq_opts_by_param files. Signal: (call_wall - high) in [0, 5). Control: (call_wall - high) > 10. Exclude sessions with range < 0.3% of close to avoid division artifacts. Primary metric: median shadow_ratio_near - median shadow_ratio_far. Falsifiable if diff <= 0 or p > 0.30.

title: High Total Open Interest Suppresses Daily Realized Range (Exploratory)
claim: Sessions in the top quintile of total open interest (dte > 0 contracts, to exclude same-day 0DTE noise) show lower realized daily range (high - low) / close than sessions in the bottom quintile, consistent with dealer long-gamma positioning absorbing directional pressure. Confidence prior: low — this is exploratory.
rationale: When dealers are net long gamma across their book, they mechanically sell into rallies and buy into declines, suppressing realized volatility. High total OI is a crude proxy for dealer gamma exposure. The main confound is that high OI may co-occur with volatile regimes (OI builds during uncertainty) rather than causing suppression. Excluding dte=0 OI reduces same-day 0DTE noise but does not eliminate the confound. Results must explicitly note whether regime co-variation is driving the finding.
testability_notes: Data: total_oi (dte>0) from param files + daily_series.parquet. Quintile split on oi_dte_gt1. Primary metric: median_range_high_oi - median_range_low_oi (expected negative). Must report both dte>0 and total-OI versions. Verdict_reason must state confound risk. Falsifiable if diff >= 0 or p > 0.30.

title: Expiry Pinning at High-OI Strikes: Fridays vs Non-Friday Sessions
claim: On Fridays (which carry both daily 0DTE and weekly series expiring simultaneously, producing higher total expiring OI), QQQ close is nearer to the nearest high-OI wall (call_wall or put_wall) than on Mon-Thu sessions, consistent with academic findings that prices cluster near high-OI strikes on heavy-expiry dates. QQQ has 0DTE options every trading day, so Friday vs Mon-Thu is the meaningful expiry-weight comparison.
rationale: Academic research (Ni, Pearson, Poteshman 2005; Augen 2009 replication studies) shows stock prices cluster near option strikes on expiration dates, with the effect stronger on weekly options expiry. QQQ has daily 0DTE every session, but Fridays add weekly series expirations producing higher aggregate expiring OI. If the pinning mechanism (dealer delta hedging collapsing toward the dominant strike near expiry) is real, Fridays should show tighter close-to-wall distances than non-Friday sessions.
testability_notes: Data: daily_series.parquet (close) + wall table (call_wall, put_wall). Signal: is_friday (dayofweek==4). Metric: min(|close - call_wall|, |close - put_wall|) / close. Primary: median_dist_friday - median_dist_non_friday (expected negative). Also report dte=0 OI quintile cut as secondary. Falsifiable if diff >= 0 or p > 0.30.

title: Prior-Day Call/Put Volume Imbalance Predicts Next-Session Return Direction (Exploratory)
claim: Sessions where prior-day call volume exceeded put volume by more than 10 percentage points (call_frac > 0.55) show a positive next-session log return bias compared to sessions where put volume dominated (call_frac < 0.45), weakly consistent with call-heavy option flow reflecting bullish positioning. This is an exploratory proxy — total EOD volume is not buyer-initiated order imbalance.
rationale: A Journal of Finance paper (Pan and Poteshman 2006) found buyer-initiated option volume predicts future stock returns. Our data provides total daily call and put volume from EOD snapshots, which cannot distinguish buyer vs seller initiated flow. The signal is therefore a noisy proxy. A key confound: 0DTE put volume spikes on volatile sessions for intraday hedging, making put-heavy days a marker of prior-day volatility rather than bearish positioning. H51 tested PCR vs next-day range (inconclusive). This tests call_frac vs next-day directional return — different outcome variable.
testability_notes: Data: daily call_vol and put_vol aggregated from qqq_opts_by_param files + daily_series.parquet. call_frac = call_vol / (call_vol + put_vol). Signal: call_frac > 0.55. Control: call_frac < 0.45. Primary metric: mean_next_return_call_heavy - mean_next_return_put_heavy. Also report same-day return as extra_metric (contemporaneous check). Loose thresholds: support p < 0.15, reject p > 0.40. Verdict must label as exploratory.

title: Top-Quintile Daily Range Autocorrelation: High-RV Days Predict High-RV Next Session
claim: Sessions in the top quintile of daily range (high-low)/close predict above-median range in the next session at a rate exceeding 60%, consistent with realized volatility autocorrelation over a 1-day lag (Hurst=0.83 confirmed in H39).
rationale: H39 confirmed Hurst exponent 0.83 for daily realized vol (long-run persistence). This tests whether the 1-day actionable lag is strong enough to trade on: does a top-quintile range day predict above-median range the next session? If so, it can gate strategies requiring elevated intraday range.
testability_notes: Data: daily_series.parquet (high, low, close). Signal: daily_range = (high-low)/close in top quintile (>= 80th percentile). Outcome: next-session range above sample median. Primary metric: win_rate_top_quintile (fraction of top-quintile days where next range > median). Test: binomial vs p=0.50. Support: win_rate > 0.60 AND p_binomial < 0.10. Reject: win_rate <= 0.50 OR p > 0.30.

title: Opening Gap Fill: Gaps > 0.5% Close Nearer to Prior Close than to Open by End of Session
claim: Sessions where the open gaps more than 0.5% away from the prior close end with the close nearer to the prior close than to the open (gap fill) at a rate exceeding 55%, consistent with mean-reversion mechanics when gaps are driven by overnight positioning rather than genuine directional information.
rationale: Classical gap-fill theory: gaps created by overnight order imbalances (not news) tend to fill as day session liquidity corrects the over-extension. Bittman and Baird discuss opening range dynamics; gap behavior is a key intraday pattern for premium sellers and swing traders. Tests whether gap fill is a statistically reliable pattern in QQQ.
testability_notes: Data: daily_series.parquet (open, close, prior close from log_return). Gap = (open - prev_close)/prev_close. Gap day: |gap| > 0.005. Gap fill: |close - prev_close| < |close - open|. Primary metric: gap_fill_rate (fraction of gap days that fill). Test: binomial vs p=0.50. Support: gap_fill_rate > 0.55 AND p_binomial < 0.10. Reject: gap_fill_rate <= 0.50 OR p > 0.30. Extra: split by gap direction (up/down) and by gap size quintile.

title: Variance Premium Sweet Spot: IV 1-1.5 Sigma Above Mean Delivers Largest Edge Over Realized Vol
claim: Sessions where iv_30d is between 1 and 1.5 standard deviations above its rolling 90-day mean deliver a larger variance premium (iv_30d - fwd_rv_20) than sessions where iv_30d is more than 2 standard deviations above mean (overextended), consistent with premium sellers having the best risk/reward in the moderate-elevated IV zone rather than at extremes.
rationale: H1 (IV vs HV spread → premium) and H28 (regime-filtered premium) confirmed the variance premium is real. Sinclair (ch 3-4) argues that extreme IV readings often coincide with actual volatility expansions that erode the premium. The 'sweet spot' thesis: moderate elevation has better signal-to-noise than extremes. Tests whether the relationship is monotone or has an optimal zone.
testability_notes: Data: daily_series.parquet (iv_30d, fwd_rv_20). Compute rolling 90-day mean and std of iv_30d. Sweet spot: iv_30d in [mean + 1*std, mean + 1.5*std]. Overextended: iv_30d > mean + 2*std. Baseline: iv_30d < mean + 0.5*std. Primary metric: mean_vp_sweetspot - mean_vp_overextended where vp = iv_30d - fwd_rv_20. Support: diff > 0.005 AND p_mannwhitney < 0.10. Reject: diff <= 0 OR p > 0.30.

title: Compound Signal: Pattern 4 AND Backwardation Both Active Predict Larger Range Than Either Alone
claim: Sessions where Pattern 4 (iv_30d rising while realized vol flat/falling) AND term structure backwardation (iv_30d > iv_60d) are simultaneously active predict larger next-session intraday range than sessions where only one signal is active, consistent with compound signals providing stronger confirmation than either signal alone.
rationale: H53 (Pattern 4 → range) SUPPORTED, H44 (backwardation → range) SUPPORTED. If both signals measure partially independent dimensions of uncertainty pricing (H53 = flow urgency, H44 = term structure stress), their conjunction should provide stronger confirmation. Tests whether compound signal adds incremental predictive value beyond either alone — a direct test of signal stacking utility.
testability_notes: Data: daily_series.parquet (iv_30d, iv_60d, log_return, high, low, close). Pattern 4: delta_iv_5d > 0.005 AND delta_rv_5d < 0.005. Backwardation: iv_30d > iv_60d. Four groups: both active, P4 only, backwardation only, neither. Primary metric: median_range_both - median_range_p4_only. Extra: compare all four groups. Support: both > p4_only by diff > 0.001 AND p_mannwhitney < 0.15. Reject: diff <= 0 OR p > 0.35.

title: Buy-the-Dip 3-Session Swing: After -1% Sessions, Cumulative 3-Session Return Is Positive
claim: After sessions where QQQ log_return falls below -1%, the cumulative return over the next 3 trading sessions is positive at a rate exceeding 55% of occurrences, consistent with short-term mean-reversion after large down moves in a structurally upward-trending market.
rationale: Baird and Natenberg discuss mean-reversion tendencies after sharp moves due to options dealer delta-hedging (buying the dip as puts gain delta). H22 confirmed asymmetric IV response to down moves. Structural mean-reversion after large down moves is a well-documented phenomenon in equity indices. Tests whether the effect is large enough to be exploitable over a 3-session horizon.
testability_notes: Data: daily_series.parquet (log_return). Signal: log_return < -0.01 (>1% down day). Outcome: cumulative 3-session return = sum of next 3 log_returns > 0. Primary metric: win_rate_positive_3d (fraction of signal days where 3d cumsum > 0). Test: binomial vs p=0.50. Support: win_rate > 0.55 AND p_binomial < 0.10. Reject: win_rate <= 0.50 OR p > 0.30. Extra: mean_3d_return, median_3d_return, n_signal_days, pct_signal_days.

title: Weekend IV Premium: Monday iv_30d Exceeds Prior-Friday iv_30d Systematically
claim: Monday iv_30d readings are systematically higher than prior-Friday iv_30d readings, reflecting an implied weekend variance premium where the market prices in uncertainty accumulated over the non-trading weekend period.
rationale: Options price time value including weekends — a 3-calendar-day weekend versus 1 trading day creates a mechanical IV adjustment at the Monday open. This is distinct from any directional signal; it tests whether the weekend premium is visible in constant-maturity IV30d. If confirmed, it has implications for Friday-vs-Monday option pricing strategies and calendar spread timing.
testability_notes: Data: daily_series.parquet (iv_30d, date). For each Monday, compute iv_change = iv_30d(Monday) - iv_30d(prior Friday). Primary metric: mean_iv_change_monday (expected positive). Test: one-sample t-test vs 0. Support: mean_change > 0.003 AND p_ttest < 0.10. Reject: mean_change <= 0 OR p > 0.30. Extra: median_iv_change_monday, n_mondays, n_fridays, pct_mondays_higher.

title: Gap Days in Backwardation Fill More Frequently Than Gap Days in Contango
claim: On gap days (|open - prev_close| > 0.5%) that occur while the IV term structure is in backwardation (iv_30d > iv_60d), the gap fill rate exceeds that of gap days in contango, consistent with elevated near-term uncertainty (backwardation) amplifying mean-reversion pressure after opening gaps.
rationale: Combines H71 (gap fill) with H44 (backwardation → elevated range and reversion). If backwardation signals near-term stress, gaps on backwardation days may be driven more by panic/urgency than genuine information, increasing the likelihood of a fill. Tests whether the regime context of the gap day predicts fill probability — a compound test of two supported signals.
testability_notes: Data: daily_series.parquet (open, close, iv_30d, iv_60d, log_return for prev_close). Gap day: |gap_pct| > 0.005. Gap fill: |close - prev_close| < |close - open|. Backwardation: iv_30d > iv_60d. Primary metric: gap_fill_rate_backwardation - gap_fill_rate_contango. Test: Fisher's exact test (2x2 table: fill/no-fill vs backw/contango). Support: diff > 0.08 AND p_fisher < 0.15. Reject: diff <= 0 OR p > 0.35.

title: Low Vol-of-Vol Entry Filter: Stable IV Environments Deliver Larger Variance Premium
claim: Sessions where the 10-day rolling standard deviation of iv_30d (vol-of-vol) is in the bottom tercile (most stable IV) show a larger realized variance premium (iv_30d - fwd_rv_20) than sessions in the top tercile (most volatile IV), consistent with Sinclair's principle that premium-selling edge is largest when IV is stable rather than rapidly oscillating.
rationale: Sinclair (ch 5-6) argues that selling vol when IV is rapidly changing is dangerous: the vol-of-vol itself represents uncertainty about the fair value of IV, making short-vol positions riskier. When vol-of-vol is low (IV is stable), the variance premium estimate is more reliable and the realized edge is historically higher. Tests whether this practical filtering rule has statistical support in the QQQ dataset.
testability_notes: Data: daily_series.parquet (iv_30d, fwd_rv_20). vol_of_vol = rolling 10-day std of iv_30d. Bottom tercile (stable): vol_of_vol <= 33rd percentile. Top tercile (volatile): vol_of_vol >= 67th percentile. Primary metric: mean_vp_stable - mean_vp_volatile where vp = iv_30d - fwd_rv_20. Support: diff > 0.005 AND p_mannwhitney < 0.10. Reject: diff <= 0 OR p > 0.30.

title: VWAP Reclaim After Open — Confirmed Cross Predicts Next-Bar-Open 30-Minute Continuation
claim: On sessions where QQQ makes a confirmed VWAP reclaim (two consecutive bars below cumulative session VWAP followed by a close above VWAP) within the 9:45–10:25 AM reclaim window, the subsequent 30 minutes starting from the next bar's open show a positive return at a rate exceeding 55% of such sessions, consistent with VWAP reclaim acting as a morning momentum confirmation signal. Entry is at the open of the bar following the signal bar to avoid same-bar execution bias.
rationale: VWAP is the institutional reference price for the session — it separates buyers who paid more than average from those who paid less. A confirmed reclaim (price was below VWAP for 2+ bars, then closes above) suggests the balance of power has shifted from sellers to buyers, and institutional algorithms tracking VWAP may provide continuation flow. The 2-bar quality filter prevents counting noisy single-bar flips around VWAP. Tests whether this morning momentum pattern has statistical support in QQQ.
testability_notes: Data: Databento 5-min OHLCV bars (data/raw/databento/qqq_5m_YYYYMM.parquet). Bar label = bar-start (confirmed: pandas resample label='left'). VWAP = cumulative typical price * volume / cumulative volume from session open. Signal: first bar T with close[T]>VWAP[T], close[T-1]<=VWAP[T-1], close[T-2]<=VWAP[T-2], bar label in 09:45-10:25. Entry: open[T+1]. Exit: close[T+6] (30-min hold). Primary: pct_continuation. Binomial vs p=0.50. Support: pct > 0.55, p < 0.10. Report n_confirmed_reclaims, n_raw_crosses, pct_held_2bars, pct_held_5bars.

title: Confirmed VWAP Breakout — High Relative Volume Predicts Larger Rest-of-Day Return (Bucket-Stratified)
claim: Within each time-of-day bucket (early: 9:45-10:25, late: 10:30-12:55), confirmed VWAP breakouts (2-bar quality filter) occurring with cumulative session volume >= 1.2x the historically-expected volume at that time-of-day (using a rolling leak-safe intraday volume profile) deliver larger rest-of-day returns from entry than breakouts at <= 0.8x expected volume, consistent with high relative volume confirming institutional participation rather than noise breakouts. Time-bucket stratification controls for the time-left confound (early breakouts have more session time remaining than late breakouts).
rationale: Volume confirmation is a foundational principle in technical analysis: breakouts on high volume are more likely to be sustained than low-volume breakouts. For VWAP breakouts specifically, high volume suggests real institutional demand rather than a momentary imbalance. The relative-volume baseline uses a time-of-day adjusted profile (not linear fraction) because intraday volume is front-loaded (~30-40% of daily volume trades in the first hour). Bucket stratification prevents the time-left confound from inflating the apparent value of early high-volume breakouts over late low-volume ones.
testability_notes: Data: Databento 5-min OHLCV + daily_series.parquet (volume for 20-day rolling avg). Signal: same quality-filtered VWAP cross as H78, window 09:45-12:55. Entry: open[T+1]. Exit: close[15:55]. Relative volume: cum_session_vol / (vol_profile[HH:MM] * daily_avg_vol_20d). Volume profile: rolling expanding mean of prior sessions (leak-safe). Groups: rel_vol>=1.2 (high) vs <=0.8 (low). Primary: mean_rod_high - mean_rod_low within each bucket and overall. Mann-Whitney. Support: diff_overall > 0.001, p < 0.10, same direction in >= 1 bucket.

title: 60-Day Variance Premium: iv_60d Exceeds 60-Day Forward Realized Volatility
claim: The 60-day constant-maturity IV (iv_60d) exceeds the subsequently realized 60-day close-to-close volatility by a positive margin on average, consistent with the variance risk premium extending beyond the 20-day horizon confirmed in H1 and H28. This is a descriptive finding about the premium level, not a predictive trading signal.
rationale: H1 and H28 confirm a variance premium at the 20-day horizon. If the premium reflects systematic risk compensation (a structural feature of option markets), it should persist at longer horizons. The 60-day tenor tests this persistence. The overlapping-window nature of 60-day forward RV means the finding is descriptive — the t-test p-value is an approximation only, and the mean sign and magnitude are the primary evidence.
testability_notes: Data: daily_series.parquet, columns iv_60d and log_return. Compute fwd_rv_60[t] = std(log_return[t+1:t+61]) * sqrt(252). vp_60d[t] = iv_60d[t] - fwd_rv_60[t]. Primary metric: mean(vp_60d). Support: mean > 0.010 (1 vol point). Reject: mean <= 0. Overlapping windows — t-test is approximate (effective N ~8 non-overlapping blocks).

title: Put-Heavy EOD Option Volume Associates with iv_30d Rise Within 2 Sessions
claim: Sessions with elevated put-to-total-volume ratio (PCR > 0.58) are associated with higher iv_30d over the following 2 sessions compared to call-heavy sessions (PCR < 0.42). This is an associative finding only — PCR may proxy for realized volatility shocks rather than being an independent predictor of IV changes.
rationale: Heavy put buying could reflect elevated protective demand, which in turn increases implied volatility on the demand side. However, 0DTE put volume spikes on volatile sessions are a confound — large down days drive both high PCR and subsequent IV rises, making same-day vol a plausible alternative explanation. Labeled as exploratory association, not structural prediction.
testability_notes: Data: call + put param files (190 overlap dates) for daily PCR; daily_series.parquet for iv_30d. Per date: pcr_vol = sum(put volume) / (sum(put vol) + sum(call vol)) across all strikes/expiries. Join with daily_series; compute iv_change_2d = iv_30d[t+2] - iv_30d[t]. Signal: pcr_vol > 0.58; control: pcr_vol < 0.42. Primary metric: mean_iv_change_put_heavy - mean_iv_change_control. Mann-Whitney U. Support: diff > 0.003 AND p < 0.10.

title: Near-Spot Short-Dated OI Concentration Predicts Next-Session Range Contraction
claim: Sessions with high adjusted-HHI concentration of open interest among short-dated (1-30 DTE) near-spot (+/-5%) options are followed by smaller next-session intraday ranges, consistent with concentrated option OI near spot creating a gravitational effect on price movement. HHI is normalized for the number of qualifying strikes to remove mechanical N-dependence.
rationale: Full-chain HHI is distorted by far-OTM strike dilution, expiry-mix variation, and newly-listed strikes after large moves. Restricting to near-spot short-dated options isolates the universe where gamma hedging effects are concentrated. Adjusted HHI normalizes for universe size. The hypothesis tests the empirical association between OI concentration and realized range without claiming knowledge of dealer position direction.
testability_notes: Data: call + put param files (190 overlap dates). Universe: |price_strike / underlying_price - 1| <= 0.05 AND dte between 1-30. Combine call + put OI per strike. adj_hhi = (raw_hhi - 1/N_k) / (1 - 1/N_k). Outcome: next-session (high - low) / close from daily_series. Compare top vs bottom quintile of adj_hhi. Mann-Whitney U (alternative=less). Support: diff < -0.001 AND p < 0.10.

title: Peak Gamma-Weighted OI Strike: Proximity Associates with Next-Day Range Contraction
claim: On sessions where the EOD close is within $3 of the strike with the highest combined (call + put) gamma-weighted OI among short-dated (1-30 DTE) near-spot (+/-5%) options, the next session intraday range is smaller than on sessions where the close is $8 or more from that peak strike. Tested as an empirical association — gross gamma-weighted OI only, no dealer position sign assumed.
rationale: Large gamma-weighted OI at a specific strike creates a coordination point for holders across all option positions, not just dealers. This is distinct from H82 (which tests OI dispersion): H83 tests whether price proximity to the single dominant strike correlates with range suppression. The hypothesis avoids net-gamma or GEX framing because dealer sign is not identifiable from listed OI data alone.
testability_notes: Data: call + put param files (190 overlap dates). Universe: same as H82 (dte 1-30, +/-5% moneyness). Per strike: gamma_oi = gamma_call * oi_call + gamma_put * oi_put. peak_strike = argmax(gamma_oi). dist_to_peak = |close - peak_strike|. Signal: dist < 3; control: dist > 8. Outcome: next-session (high-low)/close. Mann-Whitney U (alternative=less). Support: diff < -0.001 AND p < 0.10.

title: Delta-Band OI Asymmetry Predicts Next-Session Return Direction
claim: Sessions where put open interest in the 0.15-0.40 delta band (short-dated 1-30 DTE) exceeds call OI in the same delta band by more than 50% (oi_ratio > 1.5) are associated with lower next-session returns than sessions where call OI dominates (oi_ratio < 0.67). Strictly exploratory — delta-band OI aggregates directional bets, hedges, spreads, and covered writes indiscriminately.
rationale: Delta bands (0.15-0.40) are more robust than single-strike OTM comparisons: they aggregate across multiple strikes, are scale-invariant with respect to underlying price, and match standard professional skew measurement conventions (25-delta OTM). However, OI in these bands cannot isolate directional hedging demand from covered call/put activity or dealer inventory. The hypothesis tests whether the structural OI asymmetry has an empirical next-session return correlation, labeled as exploratory.
testability_notes: Data: call + put param files (190 overlap dates). Put band OI: puts with |delta| between 0.15-0.40 AND dte 1-30. Call band OI: calls with delta between 0.15-0.40 AND dte 1-30. oi_ratio = put_band_oi / call_band_oi. Signal: ratio > 1.5; control: ratio < 0.67. Outcome: next log_return from daily_series. Mann-Whitney U (alternative=less). Support (loose): diff < -0.001 AND p < 0.15.

title: Short-Dated Call OI Expansion Associates with Next-Session Positive Return
claim: Sessions where aggregate short-dated (1-30 DTE) call open interest increases by more than 5% from the prior session (excluding dates following large expiry-driven OI collapses) are associated with a higher fraction of positive next-session returns than sessions where call OI contracts by more than 5%. Strictly exploratory — call OI expansion reflects covered call writing, roll activity, and spread construction alongside directional buying; net position direction is unknown.
rationale: Call OI growth may partially capture accumulation of bullish long-call positions. However, covered call writers, spread legs, rolls, and dealer inventory changes all add to call OI without directional signal. Filtering to DTE 1-30 removes the slow-moving far-dated OI noise. Excluding dates following large OI drops (>15%) removes expiry contamination. The hypothesis is labeled exploratory — tests empirical association only.
testability_notes: Data: call param files (317 C dates available). Per date: sum call OI for dte 1-30. Consecutive date pct change. Prior-day drop filter: exclude dates where prior-session call OI dropped >15% (expiry contamination). Signal: oi_change_pct > 0.05; control: oi_change_pct < -0.05. Outcome: next log_return from daily_series. Primary: win_rate_expansion (fraction where next return > 0). Binomial vs p=0.50. Support (loose): win_rate > 0.55 AND p < 0.10.

title: Daily Leverage Effect: Down Days Predict Higher 5-Day Realized Volatility Than Equivalent Up Days
claim: After QQQ log_return days with return < -0.005, the forward 5-day realized volatility (std of next 5 log returns * sqrt(252)) is significantly higher than after days with return > +0.005, consistent with the leverage effect operating at daily frequency: price declines cause asymmetric increases in subsequent realized volatility.
rationale: Sinclair (Volatility Trading Ch. 3) documents the leverage effect as a structural feature of equity markets: when price falls, vol rises asymmetrically compared to equivalent upward moves. Two mechanisms: (1) financial leverage — as stock price falls, debt/equity rises, making equity riskier; (2) volatility feedback — traders expect higher future vol after a decline, driving demand for puts. This is the daily-frequency version, distinct from H22 which tested the intraday IV response.
testability_notes: Data: daily_series.parquet, log_return column. Compute fwd_hv_5[t] = std(log_return[t+1:t+6]) * sqrt(252). Signal: log_return < -0.005; Control: log_return > +0.005. Primary metric: mean(fwd_hv_5|signal) - mean(fwd_hv_5|control). Mann-Whitney U (alternative=greater). Support: diff > 0.003 AND p < 0.05. Key confound: negative days may have larger absolute magnitude — report median abs(return) per group.

title: Bear Regime Realized Volatility: hv_20 At Least 1.5x Higher When Price Below 200-Day MA
claim: QQQ median hv_20_cc on days when closing price is below its 200-day rolling MA is at least 1.5x the median hv_20_cc on days when price is above the 200-day MA, consistent with the empirical finding that equity index realized volatility is approximately 1.8x higher in bear market regimes.
rationale: Sinclair (Volatility Trading Ch. 3) documents bull market median vol = 12.1% vs bear market = 21.6% (~1.8x difference) for the S&P 500. The mechanism: bear markets involve elevated uncertainty, deleveraging, and increased option demand that translate to higher realized vol. For vol strategy sizing, this means position sizes should be materially smaller in bear regimes to maintain constant expected loss.
testability_notes: Data: daily_series.parquet, close and hv_20_cc columns. Compute 200-day rolling MA of close. Bull: close > ma_200. Bear: close <= ma_200. Primary metric: median_hv20_bear / median_hv20_bull. Also Mann-Whitney U (two-sided). Support: ratio > 1.50 AND p < 0.01. Insufficient: n_bear < 20. Key caveat: test window 2024-2026 likely has few bear-regime days; report n_bear explicitly.

title: Inverted IV Term Structure Predicts iv_30d Decline Within 20 Sessions
claim: On days where iv_30d exceeds iv_90d by more than 5% (inverted term structure), iv_30d is lower 20 trading days later more than 58% of the time, consistent with elevated front-month IV mean-reverting toward the back end of the term structure after a volatility spike.
rationale: Stein (1989) showed that if volatility mean-reverts, front-month IV must decay toward long-run vol faster than back-month IV. Sinclair (Ch. 5) confirms: inverted term structure indicates vol elevation above long-run mean. The practical implication is that front-month IV should decline after inversion resolves. This is mechanistically distinct from H44 (which tests whether inversion predicts larger intraday range) — H88 tests the direction of future IV change.
testability_notes: Data: daily_series.parquet, iv_30d and iv_90d. Signal: iv_30d > iv_90d * 1.05. Outcome: iv_30d[t+20] < iv_30d[t] (binary). Primary metric: pct_iv30d_declines_20d. Binomial test vs p=0.50. Support: pct > 0.58 AND p < 0.10. Insufficient: n < 30. Caveat: forward iv_30d windows overlap (each window shares ~10 days with adjacent). p-value approximate.

title: Normalized Variance Premium: iv_30d Exceeds 20-Day Forward Realized Vol by 15-35% on Average
claim: The variance premium expressed as a fraction of iv_30d — (iv_30d - fwd_rv_20) / iv_30d — averages between 0.15 and 0.35 across the test window, confirming the structural 30% overpayment of implied versus realized volatility documented empirically for equity index options.
rationale: Sinclair (Volatility Trading Ch. 5): 'On average, IV is approximately 30% higher than realized vol. Equivalently, variance swaps always overpay.' H1 confirmed the premium exists; H80 tested absolute magnitude at 60-day horizon. H89 tests the normalized ratio (premium / IV level) which is the invariant form of the book claim — it should hold regardless of the absolute IV level in the test window.
testability_notes: Data: daily_series.parquet, iv_30d and fwd_rv_20. Compute norm_vp = (iv_30d - fwd_rv_20) / iv_30d. Exclude rows where iv_30d < 0.05. Primary metric: mean(norm_vp). Support: mean in [0.10, 0.40]. Reject: mean <= 0 or > 0.50. Inconclusive: positive but outside support range. Overlapping windows — t-test p-value approximate.

title: IV Percentile Rank Filter: High Trailing Percentile Delivers Larger Variance Premium
claim: Days where iv_30d is above its trailing 252-day 75th percentile deliver a significantly larger subsequent variance premium (iv_30d - fwd_rv_20) than days where iv_30d is in the 25th-75th percentile range, confirming that elevated IV relative to recent history is a stronger short-vol entry signal than absolute IV level.
rationale: Sinclair (Volatility Trading Ch. 4) introduces the volatility cone: 'if ATM IV plots above the historical max cone for that horizon, the option is historically expensive.' The key insight is RELATIVE expense to recent history, not absolute level. H28 tested absolute IV level regime (15-20% being the sweet spot) and was REJECTED. H90 uses a trailing rolling percentile rank — regime-invariant — which is the correct operationalization of the volatility cone concept.
testability_notes: Data: daily_series.parquet, iv_30d and fwd_rv_20. Compute 252-day rolling p75 and p25 of iv_30d. High group: iv_30d > p75. Mid group: iv_30d between p25 and p75. Primary metric: mean_vp_high - mean_vp_mid. Mann-Whitney U (alternative=greater). Support: diff > 0.005 AND p < 0.10. Need 252-day warmup, so first ~250 rows excluded from signal dates.

title: Volatility Shock Half-Life: hv_20 Reverts to Trailing Median Within 10-50 Trading Days After Spike
claim: After hv_20_cc crosses above its trailing 252-day 80th percentile (new spike event), the median number of trading days until hv_20_cc falls below the trailing 252-day 50th percentile is between 10 and 50 trading days, quantifying the empirical mean-reversion half-life documented as 30-60 days in the volatility literature.
rationale: Sinclair (Volatility Trading Ch. 5) states: 'VIX satisfies mean-reversion — fading VIX spikes above 30 has positive expectation historically. Vol mean reverts with approximately 30-60 day half-life.' H39 confirmed that realized vol is positively autocorrelated (Hurst > 0.5), but did not quantify the reversion speed after a spike. H91 provides the actionable metric: how long does it actually take for vol to revert to the median?
testability_notes: Data: daily_series.parquet, hv_20_cc. Identify new spike events: first bar where hv_20_cc > trailing 252-day p80 after >= 5 consecutive bars below p80. For each event, count days until hv_20_cc < trailing p50. Primary metric: median_days_to_revert. Support: 10-50. Reject: > 60 or never reverts. Insufficient: n_spike_events < 5. Report n_events, pct_reverted_within_30d, pct_reverted_within_60d.

title: GARCH(1,1) Forecast Outperforms EWMA(lambda=0.94) for 20-Day Realized Vol Prediction
claim: The GARCH(1,1) one-day-ahead volatility forecast (garch_vol, already computed) achieves lower RMSE against subsequent 20-day forward realized vol (fwd_rv_20) than an EWMA(lambda=0.94) forecast computed from the same daily returns, confirming the theoretical prediction that GARCH mean reversion adds forecast value over EWMA's permanent-shock assumption.
rationale: Sinclair (Volatility Trading Ch. 4): 'EWMA is IGARCH with no mean reversion — treats vol shocks as permanent. GARCH(1,1) is strictly better because it includes mean reversion.' EWMA(0.94) is the RiskMetrics standard. H4 tested GARCH as a straddle entry signal (inconclusive). H92 tests raw RMSE comparison — the direct mechanistic claim from the book about forecast quality.
testability_notes: Data: daily_series.parquet, garch_vol (one-step-ahead GARCH forecast), log_return, fwd_rv_20. Compute EWMA variance: var_t = 0.94 * var_{t-1} + 0.06 * r^2_{t-1}, then ewma_vol = sqrt(var_t). Compare RMSE(garch_vol, fwd_rv_20) vs RMSE(ewma_vol, fwd_rv_20). Primary metric: rmse_ratio = RMSE_GARCH / RMSE_EWMA. Paired t-test on squared errors. Support: ratio < 0.95 AND p < 0.10.

title: Variance Premium Larger in Bull Regime: Price Above 200-Day MA Delivers Higher iv_30d - fwd_rv_20
claim: The variance premium (iv_30d - fwd_rv_20) is higher on average when QQQ price is above its 200-day rolling MA than when below it, because bear-regime realized volatility is more frequently elevated (reducing the gap between implied and realized vol and thereby shrinking the short-vol edge).
rationale: Sinclair (Volatility Trading Ch. 3): 'bear market vol = 21.6% vs bull = 12.1%.' When vol is structurally higher and more frequently realized, the variance premium (IV - RV) should be smaller or even negative. Bull regimes have lower baseline realized vol, allowing implied vol to systematically exceed realized vol more reliably. H1 confirmed premium exists overall; H93 tests whether the premium is regime-dependent in the expected direction.
testability_notes: Data: daily_series.parquet, close, iv_30d, fwd_rv_20. Compute ma_200 = rolling(200).mean() of close. vp_20d = iv_30d - fwd_rv_20. Bull: close > ma_200; Bear: close <= ma_200. Primary metric: mean_vp_bull - mean_vp_bear. Mann-Whitney U (alternative=greater). Support: diff > 0.003 AND p < 0.10. Insufficient: n_bear < 20.

title: Front-End Term Structure Slope (7d/30d IV) Predicts Next-Session Range
claim: When the 7-day implied volatility (iv_7d) exceeds the 30-day IV (iv_30d), placing the front end of the term structure in backwardation, the next session realized range ((high-low)/close) is significantly larger than on days when the front end is in contango (iv_7d <= iv_30d). Short-end backwardation signals near-term vol priced above structural level.
rationale: The 7-day IV is the market composite estimate of near-term realized vol for the current week. When it exceeds the 30-day IV, market makers are pricing an imminent vol event — elevated intraday risk for 0DTE and short-dated strategies. This is orthogonal to the 30d/90d slope already tested (H44, H88): those test medium-term term structure; this tests the front-end weekly signal.
testability_notes: Daily backtest on QQQ 2024-2026. Load qqq_ivx.parquet for 7d IV Mean. Signal: iv_7d > iv_30d. Outcome: next-session (high-low)/close. Mann-Whitney U test. Falsified if median range in backwardation is not larger than contango.

title: ATM Put-Call IV Spread (IVX 30d) Elevated Above Rolling Median Associates with Lower Next-Session Returns
claim: When the IVX-derived 30d put IV exceeds the 30d call IV by more than its 90-day rolling median, the next-session QQQ log return is lower on average than on days when the put-call IV spread is at or below median. This ATM put-call spread reflects near-term defensive demand priced into the market composite IV surface.
rationale: The IVX data provides put IV and call IV separately at each tenor from the data provider interpolated surface. Unlike chain-derived 25-delta skew (H50, H52 — both rejected), this measures the ATM composite put vs call IV directly. When the market prices 30d puts above calls by an above-median margin, the data provider model is reflecting elevated downside demand. Associative finding only — no dealer or institutional intent claimed.
testability_notes: Daily backtest on QQQ 2024-2026. Load qqq_ivx.parquet for 30d IV Call and 30d IV Put. Signal: (iv_put_30d - iv_call_30d) > 90-day rolling median of the same spread. Outcome: next-session log_return. Mann-Whitney U (alternative=less). Falsified if mean return is not lower in high-spread sessions.

title: Bootstrapped Forward Vol Inversion (30d→60d) Associates with Larger 5-Session Realized Range
claim: When the bootstrapped forward implied volatility for the 30d-to-60d window (derived from iv_30d and iv_60d) is lower than spot iv_30d, the forward volatility curve is inverted at the short end — indicating risk is concentrated in the near term. On such dates, the median realized range over the next 5 sessions is larger than on dates when the forward curve is normal.
rationale: The forward vol sigma_fwd = sqrt((iv_60d^2 * 60 - iv_30d^2 * 30) / 30). When sigma_fwd < iv_30d, the market prices the next 30 days more expensively than the subsequent 30 days — near-term risk dominates. This is different from the 30d/90d slope (H44, H88) which tests a longer span. The 30-60d forward specifically extracts information about where risk concentrates on the curve. Practical use: shorten trade duration on short-vol positions when forward curve inverts.
testability_notes: Daily backtest on QQQ 2024-2026. daily_series has iv_30d and iv_60d. Compute fwd_vol_30_60 = sqrt(max((iv_60d^2*60 - iv_30d^2*30)/30, 0.0001)). Signal: fwd_vol_30_60 < iv_30d. Outcome: rolling(5).mean().shift(-5) on daily range. Mann-Whitney U (alternative=greater). Falsified if inverted forward curve does not associate with larger 5-session range.

title: IV Velocity (5-Day Rate of Change) Predicts Next-Session Realized Range Direction
claim: When iv_30d has risen more than 10% over the prior 5 trading sessions (rapid IV expansion), the next session realized range is larger than the median. When iv_30d has fallen more than 8% over the prior 5 sessions (rapid IV compression), the next session range is smaller than the median. IV velocity captures regime transitions better than IV level alone.
rationale: IV level is extensively exploited (H1, H89, H90, H93). IV rate of change captures transition dynamics: rising IV indicates expanding sessions are ongoing; falling IV indicates entry into a quiet period. This is a timing filter orthogonal to level — a trader might combine H1 (VP exists) with H97 (avoid entry while IV still rising, wait for velocity to peak and roll).
testability_notes: Daily backtest on QQQ 2024-2026. Compute iv_vel_5d = iv_30d.pct_change(5). Signal groups: rising (vel > 0.10) vs falling (vel < -0.08). Outcome: next-session (high-low)/close, shift(-1). Mann-Whitney U. Falsified if rising-IV sessions do not show larger next-session range than falling-IV sessions.

title: Variance Premium Conditional on Term Structure Contango: VP Is Larger When Curve Is Normal
claim: The variance premium (iv_30d minus forward realized vol over next 20 sessions) is larger and more consistently positive when the term structure is in contango (iv_30d < iv_90d) than when it is flat or inverted. Term structure slope predicts variance premium capture quality, not just its average existence.
rationale: H1 demonstrates VP exists on average. H90 found high-IV-percentile associates with smaller VP (market correctly prices spikes). H93 found VP is larger in bull regime. This hypothesis tests a different conditioning variable: does the shape of the IV curve predict whether the premium will be realized? In contango the market is pricing normal term structure — near-term risk is proportionate. In inversion the elevated front-end often means realized vol will follow IV up, compressing the premium.
testability_notes: Daily backtest on QQQ 2024-2026. vp_20d = iv_30d - fwd_rv_20. Condition: contango (iv_30d < iv_90d) vs inverted (iv_30d >= iv_90d). Compare mean VP in each group. Mann-Whitney U (alternative=greater). Falsified if mean VP in contango is not larger than in inverted regime.

title: EOD Bid-Ask Spread Percentile Predicts Next-Session Realized Volatility
claim: When the QQQ EOD relative bid-ask spread (ask-bid)/close is in the top 20th percentile of its rolling 60-day distribution, the next-session 20-day historical volatility is higher than when the spread is in the bottom 20th percentile. Wide EOD spreads signal market maker uncertainty and associate with higher realized volatility ahead.
rationale: Bid-ask spread is a direct market microstructure signal. When market makers widen quotes, their vol estimate is uncertain — typically ahead of elevated realized vol sessions. The EOD snapshot in daily_series (bid/ask columns) is not the intraday spread, but it reflects the closing market maker stance. Wide spreads also directly impair option fill quality, so this signal has dual utility: session quality and execution quality warning.
testability_notes: Daily backtest on QQQ 2024-2026. spread_pct = (ask-bid)/close. Rolling 60-day percentile rank. High spread (rank > 0.80) vs low spread (rank < 0.20). Outcome: hv_20_cc shifted by -1 day (next-session vol reading). Mann-Whitney U (alternative=greater). Note: EOD spread is a regime proxy, not intraday fill estimate. Falsified if high-spread days do not associate with higher next-session HV.

title: Overnight Gap Magnitude Predicts Same-Session Realized Range (0DTE Entry Confirmation)
claim: Sessions with large overnight gaps (|open/prev_close - 1| > 0.5%) have a significantly higher same-session realized range ((high-low)/close) than sessions with small gaps (<0.1%). This provides a go/no-go confirmation filter for 0DTE short straddle entries at market open: large-gap opens associate with expanded intraday range and higher gamma risk for short-straddle sellers.
rationale: H14 showed that 0DTE straddles sold at open outperform those sold at noon on average. However, large-gap opens expose the seller to immediate realized vol from the gap itself. The overnight gap is the most direct pre-trade indicator available from daily data about whether intraday range will expand. Small-gap opens (quiet open) give the short-straddle seller a better starting point with less immediate gamma risk. This hypothesis tests whether gap-filtering can refine H14 entries.
testability_notes: Daily backtest on QQQ 2024-2026. gap_pct = abs(open/close.shift(1) - 1). Groups: large (gap > 0.005) vs small (gap < 0.001). Outcome: same-session (high-low)/close. Mann-Whitney U (alternative=greater). Falsified if large-gap sessions do not show significantly larger intraday range than small-gap sessions.
